name: Identity, sign-in & provisioning
intro: One identity namespace: company team members. Gong has no end-customer login at all. External buyers never sign in; they only receive shared call links. Sign-in methods can be mixed per company, and provisioning from an identity provider drives seats, permission profiles, consent profiles and data-capture settings through group assignments.

fields.What: Gong-managed username and password, with password change and reset. Sessions end automatically after two weeks.
fields.Data: Supabase Auth owns the password hash. `users(id, company_id, email, first_name, last_name, title, manager_id, status, created_at)`.
fields.Ui: Sign-in page, reset-password page, change-password in My settings.

fields.What: OAuth sign-in through Google, Microsoft or Salesforce. Salesforce sign-in needs a Salesforce admin to install Gong's external client app. Session length follows the provider's own policy (10 hours to 90 days).
fields.Ui: Provider buttons on sign-in page; admin toggle per method.

fields.What: Okta, Rippling and OneLogin via SAML, any other SAML provider, and OIDC. Default idle logout is 30 minutes; customisable for SAML.
fields.Note: Enterprise-sales feature. Irrelevant for a field-sales team that signs in on phones; parked at P3.

fields.What: An admin can enable any combination of sign-in methods at once; nothing forces one method.
Five failed sign-in attempts lock the account for 60 minutes.
fields.Data: `login_attempts(email, ip, succeeded, created_at)`; lock computed from last 5 failures.

fields.What: Team members sync from Okta, Entra ID, OneLogin, Rippling or Salesforce. Mandatory synced fields are first name, last name, job title and manager; the manager field builds the reporting hierarchy. Deactivating in the IdP deactivates in Gong.

Each IdP group maps to an assignment that sets seats, a permission profile per workspace, credit profile, data-capture settings and consent profile. Two update modes: automatic (Gong mirrors the IdP; admins cannot edit those fields in Gong) and manual (only name and manager keep syncing; everything else is set once and can drift).
fields.Data: `provisioning_assignments(id, company_id, idp_group, seats jsonb, permission_profile_by_workspace jsonb, credit_profile_id, capture_setting, consent_profile_id, update_mode)`
fields.Api: Applied by the SCIM handler on group membership change
fields.Note: Older plans capped this at 8 assignments (Coaching plan) — see https://help.gong.io/docs/plans-and-seats

fields.What: A team member has a primary and additional email addresses so calls and emails from aliases match the same person. Basis: help article titled 'About primary and additional email address' exists in the index; content not read.

features.name: Sign in to several company instances

fields.What: One person can belong to more than one Gong company instance and switch between them. Basis: article 'Enable log in to multiple Gong instances' in the index; content not read.
fields.Note: Relevant to you: as an agency running several client teams, a membership table from day one avoids a painful migration.

fields.What: Gong has no phone-number or one-time-code sign-in; every method assumes a work email. Door-to-door reps often have only a personal phone. Proposal: SMS one-time-code sign-in as a peer route to email.
fields.Source: Absence inferred from https://help.gong.io/docs/set-sign-in-method (no phone method listed)
fields.Decision: Do your reps sign in with work email, personal phone, or both? ______

decisions: **Which sign-in methods ship first?** Gong ships five families; a field team likely needs one or two. Email+password is the floor.

**One company per user, or memberships?** Gong supports multiple instances per person. If you will run the system for several client sales teams, decide now whether a person can belong to more than one.
unverified: **MFA, enforced SSO and SSO exceptions.** The sign-in article does not cover them.
**What happens to seats and data when a user is deprovisioned.** The provisioning article does not say.

name: Company structure: workspaces, teams, seats
intro: Gong splits one company into workspaces (separate data and configuration, shared integrations) and builds the team hierarchy from each person's manager. Licensing is a core seat plus application seats per person; people without a seat are free 'Collaborators'.

fields.What: A workspace divides the instance by business line, region or use case. Calls live in the call owner's home workspace; emails live in every participant's workspace. Per-workspace: permission profiles, trackers, topics, call categories, scorecards, custom vocabulary, retention and automation rules. Shared: integrations, SSO, team members, accounts, privacy (except retention), API access.
fields.Data: `workspaces(id, company_id, name, retention_days)`; `calls.workspace_id`; workspace_id on every per-workspace config table.

fields.What: Users are not assigned to one workspace. Without a permission profile in a workspace they see only its homepage and calls shared with them, where they were mentioned, or where feedback was requested.
Users can move calls to another workspace; emails and texts cannot be moved in product. Moving a person does not move their history.
Each person has a manager; the reporting tree drives 'my direct and indirect reports' scopes everywhere (calls, deals, coaching stats, forecast).
fields.Data: `users.manager_id`; recursive CTE or materialised `user_ancestors(user_id, ancestor_id, depth)`
fields.Ui: Team member panel manager picker; org tree.
fields.Note: Your sales coach system already has agents and managers; this is the generalisation (managers of managers).

fields.What: Current model: Gong Foundation is the required core license; Enable Essentials, Forecast Essentials, Gong Forecast, Gong Engage and Data Cloud are application seats on top. Seats are toggled per person or in bulk; admin panel shows used vs available.
fields.Ui: Team members table with seat icons; seat usage panel.

fields.What: A team member with no seat is a Collaborator: free, limited access (can receive shares, comments, feedback requests).
Eligible companies buy more seats from the admin panel; usable immediately, prorated to term end, invoice in 2–3 days.
Admins update many team members at once from a CSV file. Basis: article 'Make bulk changes via a CSV file' in index; columns not read.
Enterprise plans include sandboxes for testing configuration. Basis: legacy Enterprise plan lists sandboxes; FAQ article exists.

decisions: **Do you need workspaces at all?** Gong's use cases are business lines, regions, keeping recruiting calls private. For one sales org, a single workspace with teams is enough; adding `workspace_id` later is a migration across every config table.
**Do you sell by seat?** If this becomes a product you sell to other sales teams, Gong's core+application seat model is the reference; if it stays internal, skip seats entirely.
unverified: **Exact Collaborator capabilities.** The plans article says only 'limited access'.
**Workspace limits on older plans.** Numbers not given beyond legacy Coaching (3) and Enterprise (200).

name: Permission profiles & data access
intro: Access is a named permission profile per user per workspace. Each data domain (calls, emails, deals, coaching stats, insights, forecast) has its own scope: all / my manager's team / my reports / my own / specific teams. Actions (score, delete, trim, share externally, download) are separate toggles. Many toggles require a specific seat.

fields.What: Admins define profiles and assign one per user per workspace.
fields.Data: `permission_profiles(id, workspace_id, name, settings jsonb)`; `workspace_profiles(user_id, workspace_id, profile_id)`
fields.Api: `GET/POST/PUT /api/admin/permission-profiles`; Gong exposes list/get/create/update profile and list profile users

fields.What: Calls on/off; then all calls, or: calls they participated in, calls their direct and indirect reports participated in; advanced: calls of anyone on their manager's team, calls from specific teams; plus account-based access.
fields.Note: This is the single most important RLS function in the system; every list, search and stat goes through it.

fields.What: Same scope ladder as calls, applied to captured emails.

features.name: Deals, coaching, insights and forecast scopes

fields.What: Each has the ladder: all / manager's teams / reports / own / specific teams. Coaching scope governs Coaching inbox and Coaching metrics; insights scope governs Team, Initiatives and Market pages.

Score calls; override scores (including AI's); view all answered scorecards regardless of visibility; download media; share calls with customers; manually schedule and upload; record on mobile; set owned calls private; trim owned calls; delete calls; delete emails.
fields.Data: `settings.actions = {score, override_score, view_all_scorecards, download, share_external, upload, mobile_record, set_private, trim, delete_calls, delete_emails}`
fields.Api: Checked server-side on each mutating route

fields.What: Per-page gates: Engage analytics, Conversations (search, library), Deals (create/edit/delete boards), Forecast admin, Dashboards, Accounts, Coaching, Insights, Activity, mobile Business pulse, AI Builder.

Separate grants for: general business settings, Theme Spotter analyses, tracker settings, company agents/skills/automations, AI Data Extractor, scorecards and trainings, credits, dashboards, metrics and targets.
fields.Note: Gong separates Tech admin (integrations, recording) from Business admin (content and AI config).

fields.What: Grant or remove an individual user's access to a specific call outside their profile scope.
Some toggles only work when the user also holds the right seat (e.g. score calls needs Enable Essentials; forecast needs Gong Forecast).
Access to calls and emails tied to accounts the person can access; account access is 'assigned accounts' (own + reports' accounts + contacts), all, or none.

decisions: **How many roles do you actually need?** Gong's model is a full matrix. A rep/manager/admin preset trio built on the same JSON settings shape gives you Gong's flexibility later without building the editor now.
unverified: **Exact API path for get/create/update permission profile.** The index lists the operations without paths.

name: Email & calendar capture
intro: Calendar connection is what makes automatic meeting recording possible: Gong scans calendars to decide what to record. Email import feeds deal timelines and AI. Connection is company-wide (admin) or user-by-user.

fields.What: After Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 is connected, Gong scans each recorded user's calendar for meetings with a conference URL. Skips: private events, meetings created less than 30 minutes before start, meetings hosted outside the company, and internal meetings when excluded.
fields.Data: `calendar_events(id, user_id, ical_uid, title, start_at, end_at, organizer_email, conference_url, is_private, is_internal, scheduled_recording_id)`
fields.Api: Google Calendar watch + Microsoft Graph subscriptions → `POST /api/webhooks/calendar`
fields.Ui: Upcoming meetings list on Home with record/skip.

fields.What: Google Workspace and Office 365 can be connected once by an admin for everyone, or per user. Admins can restrict which mailboxes Gong may access. On-premise and cloud Exchange variants exist.
fields.Data: `mail_connections(id, company_id, user_id null, provider, scope in ('company','user'), token_ref, status)`
fields.Ui: Admin > Data capture > Email & calendar; My settings > Connect calendar.

fields.What: Imports subject, body, timestamps, recipients and metadata of customer emails; shown in deal and account activity timelines.
fields.Data: `emails(id, workspace_id, thread_id, subject, body_text, sent_at, direction)`; `email_participants(email_id, address, role, user_id, contact_id)`

fields.What: Admins list internal domains (to classify calls internal/external) and configure domains, addresses and phrases that must never be imported. Public email domains and default exclusion terms ship pre-filled.

features.name: Unrecorded meetings still count as activity

fields.What: Meetings not recorded still appear with date, invitees and description, and count as deal activity. Private ones do not.
Revenue Graph captures SMS (participants and body) and LinkedIn messages alongside calls and emails.
Non-conversation buyer signals posted by partner tools: document signed, content viewed or shared, website visit, custom actions.
fields.Data: `digital_interactions(id, account_id, contact_id, kind, payload jsonb, occurred_at)`

decisions: **Does your field team use calendars at all?** Door-to-door sessions are not calendar events. If not, calendar capture is irrelevant to v1 and recordings start from the phone (F6.4).
unverified: **How emails and calls are matched to contacts and accounts.** Matching logic articles exist but were not read; see M29.

name: Web-conference recording
intro: Two recording methods: a bot that joins as a participant, or native recording (Zoom) that Gong fetches afterwards. Ownership of each call is decided by a strict rule order before and after the call. Fifty-plus skip codes explain every unrecorded meeting.

fields.What: A virtual participant joins the meeting and records audio (and optionally video). Bot display name is selectable: 'Gong Recorder', '[Company] Recorder by Gong', 'Gong AI Notetaker', 'Gong Notetaker'.
fields.Data: `scheduled_recordings(id, calendar_event_id, meeting_url, provider, method='bot', status, skip_code, bot_session_id)`
fields.Api: Worker dispatches bot at start-1 min; `POST /api/webhooks/recorder`
fields.Decision: Build a meeting bot yourself or buy one (a recording-bot API vendor)? Gong built its own; this is months of work per provider. ______

fields.What: Zoom records in-platform; Gong retrieves the file afterwards. No bot appears. ON AIR shows ~15 minutes before (5 for back-to-back on a personal room) until end, up to 6 hours after scheduled end.
Zoom, Google Meet, Webex, Microsoft Teams, GoToMeeting, Amazon Chime, RingCentral Meetings/Video, join.me, Uber Conference, Appointlet; admin chooses which providers to record.

Which meetings to record (organised by a recorded member, or organised by anyone with a recorded member invited); record internal calls yes/no; audio+video or audio only; minimum duration to import (default 30 s; 3 s fixed for Gong Dialer). Per-member settings override company settings.
fields.Data: `recording_settings(workspace_id, record_scope, record_internal bool, record_video bool, min_duration_sec int default 30)`
fields.Note: Min-duration matters for your use case: a 10-second door answer that ends in 'not interested' should probably still be stored as an attempt, not analysed.

fields.What: Each team member has a data capture setting; 'Never record' on any participant blocks recording even if the bot is invited.
fields.Note: The exact list of mode names was not confirmed; 'never record' is confirmed.

fields.What: Invite the recorder or use Home > More actions > Schedule new recording with a URL. 'Now' can take up to ten minutes to start. Users can stop or cancel from Home.
fields.Ui: Schedule dialog; stop button on ON AIR card.

fields.What: Recording and processing is limited to six hours; longer calls skip with TOO_LONG.

Before the call, first match wins: scheduled via Gong Home → meeting URL on a member's profile → provider API says whose URL → organizer is a recorded member → invited recorded member (most recorded calls wins). After: planned owner attended → else host matched by name (or screen-sharer) → else an attending member; with several, planned owner keeps it. Recalculated if the event changes.
fields.Api: `resolveOwner(call)` pure function with tests per rule
fields.Ui: Owner shown on call page; editable via call details.

fields.What: Every unrecorded meeting gets a reason code: e.g. BAD_SCHEDULE, CALL_BLOCKLISTED, COMPLIANCE_USER_REQUEST, DENIED_ENTRY, HAS_DO_NOT_RECORD_USERS, INTERNAL_MEETING, MEETING_LOCKED, NO_ATTENDEES, NO_COMPANY_PARTICIPANTS, OBSOLETE_CALL (organised within 20 min), PASSWORD_REQUIRED, TOO_LONG, TOO_SHORT, WEB_CLIENT_DISABLED, plus meeting-level codes (ALL_DAY_EVENT, NO_URL, PRIVATE_OR_CONFIDENTIAL, NO_CRM_MATCH) and dialer codes (BUSY_LINE, CARRIER_BLOCKED, RECORDING_RESTRICTED).
fields.Ui: Call status report; tooltip on skipped meetings.
fields.Note: Worth copying as a pattern even for door sessions: a closed reason list for 'session not analysed' makes the funnel honest.

fields.What: If nobody from the company joins, the bot leaves and discards the recording (NO_COMPANY_PARTICIPANTS); if nobody joins at all, NO_ATTENDEES.
A Gong app inside Zoom shows insights during the call. Basis: articles 'Gong live insights for Zoom' and 'About the Gong app for Zoom' in index; content not read.

decisions: **Are video calls in scope for v1?** Your sessions are door-to-door, voice and video. Door and phone capture are under your control; video needs a bot (F5.1), which is the most expensive single item in this module.
unverified: **Full list of per-member capture modes.** Only 'Never record' is confirmed.

name: Telephony, dialer imports, mobile & uploads
intro: Phone calls are imported, not joined: Gong pulls audio and metadata from 30+ telephony providers via API, or via Salesforce activities as a fallback. In-person meetings are recorded on the phone app. Anything else can be uploaded as a file.

fields.What: Connects to provider APIs (8x8, Aircall, Dialpad, RingCentral, Twilio Flex, Zoom Phone, Talkdesk, Five9, Genesys, Outreach, Salesloft, HubSpot and ~20 more) and downloads recordings plus call attempts, including calls without recordings. Recording must be on in the telephony system and the user set to import.
For some dialers, Gong finds recordings through Salesforce activities the dialer creates after each call.
fields.Api: Salesforce query on Task with recording URL

fields.What: Upload WAV, MP3, MP4, MKV or FLAC up to 2 GB from the quick-actions menu or Conversations > Search. Analysis takes up to an hour; user can rename, make private or delete while processing; email on completion. Uploaded calls have no participant metadata; speakers are named afterwards.
fields.Note: The cheapest capture path. It is also the fallback when anything else fails.

fields.What: Gong app > Actions > Record a meeting. Meetings starting within 2 hours are offered for linking, or SKIP to record unlinked. Record/pause/resume, stop, name, optionally link account/opportunity/contacts, save; then upload, analyse, transcribe. Audio only. Needs 'manually schedule & upload' permission.
fields.Ui: Record screen with big record/pause, timer, save sheet.
fields.Note: This is the closest Gong feature to a door-to-door session. Gong treats it as a side feature; for you it is the main capture path.

fields.What: On supported iPhones a Live Activity shows recording status and elapsed time while the app is backgrounded or the phone is locked; tapping returns to the recording.

features.name: Recents with upload and analysis status

fields.What: The mobile Recents tab shows each recent recording's upload and analysis state.

features.name: Call outcomes after a mobile recording

fields.What: After a call the rep adds a call outcome to track the result and plan follow-ups.
fields.Note: Maps directly to your funnel: door knocked → presentation → sold.

features.name: Mobile phone calls via Gong Connect

fields.What: Virtual phone numbers that let reps' mobile calls be captured. Basis: data-capture article lists 'Gong Connect: virtual phone numbers for the Gong dialer'; 'Capture mobile calls with Gong Connect' article not read.

features.name: Create call via API with media

fields.What: External systems create a call record then attach media.

Gong's mobile article says nothing about recording without signal or resuming failed uploads. Field reps lose signal. Proposal: record to local storage first, upload in chunks when online, never lose a session.
fields.Data: (if taken) client-side queue; server dedupe by `client_recording_id`
fields.Decision: Ship offline recording at launch, or require signal? ______

decisions: **Which capture paths ship first?** Mobile in-person recording plus file upload covers door-to-door. Telephony import covers voice. Bots cover video.
**Do you own the phone side?** If reps call from their own phones, capture needs either a dialer you provide (M25) or an import from whatever phone system they use.
unverified: **Mobile recording consent handling, max length, Android background behaviour.** The mobile article does not cover them.
**How telephony calls are matched to users (extension or number).** Not described.

name: Recording consent
intro: Consent is configured as profiles assigned by team or region, so reps never decide per call. Gong's tools: an audio announcement, a hosted consent page in front of the meeting link (optionally enforced), opt-out ('join without recording'), and a pre-call email.

fields.What: Multiple profiles, each assigned to teams or regions; stricter rule applies when participants are in different regions.

A prompt plays when participants join; per participant or once; language, voice and text configurable; can be skipped for people who already consented on the consent page. Phone calls require a verbal notice.

features.name: Hosted consent page, enabled or enforced

fields.What: Meeting links redirect to a branded consent page. Enabled: bypassers may still be recorded. Enforced: recorded only if all participants consent. Localised to browser language.
fields.Ui: Branded page with logo and text.

fields.What: Participants can decline and still join; the call is not recorded (skip code COMPLIANCE_USER_REQUEST). Not available on every provider.
Sent 10–20 minutes before the meeting; subject, body, logo and privacy link customisable; the recording notice itself cannot be removed.
Dynamic links (per meeting, via calendar add-on) are most secure but don't support personal rooms or Calendly; static links support those but need setup.
The Call status report shows how many participants opted out.
For dialer calls, recording can be auto, manual-only or prohibited per country or area code.

Gong's mobile recording article gives no consent guidance for in-person meetings. A door-to-door session records a homeowner who never saw a consent page. Proposal: a required consent step before recording starts (rep taps 'customer agreed', optionally records the verbal yes as the first seconds of audio).
fields.Ui: Consent confirm before record button activates.
fields.Decision: What consent rule applies to recorded door visits in the markets you operate in? This is a legal question for you, not a design one. ______

decisions: **Is recording consent a launch blocker?** For in-person recording it likely is. Check the law where your reps work before any session is recorded.
unverified: **Default values of any consent setting.** The article states none.
**Per-country rule presets.** Gong publishes no country table.

name: Transcription, speakers & language
intro: Every call becomes a speaker-attributed transcript. Diarization differs by recording type (stereo phone = one speaker per channel; mono and conference = split by voice). Opted-in users can have voice prints. 70+ languages are transcribed; transcripts and AI outputs can be translated.

fields.What: Every recorded call is transcribed with timestamps per segment.
fields.Decision: Which speech-to-text engine (hosted API vs your local model)? You plan local STT on the MacBook; production needs a server path. ______

fields.What: Conference and mono calls are split by voice differences, with a second pass for short utterances; stereo phone calls treat each channel as one speaker.

Conference speakers are matched by display name (full or unique short forms) or phone number to invitees; stereo phone: one channel to the Gong user, the other to the external party; mono phone: transcript decides which side is the company, voice ID as fallback. Shared Zoom rooms become 'Speaker 1/2'.
fields.Note: For a door session (one phone, two voices, mono) the hard question is which voice is the rep. Voice ID (F8.4) is the reliable answer.

fields.What: Admin enables, each user opts in. Up to five short samples (ideally mono calls with 2+ minutes of speech), continually replaced. Once enough exist, earlier calls are re-analysed. No voice data for non-users; no voice-print file retained.

features.name: Rename speakers on the call page

fields.What: A participant or admin edits speaker names (documented for Zoom-native and uploaded calls).
72 language entries (71 distinct), including Filipino (Philippines). Language detected automatically; if wrong, users set spoken languages in My Profile and reprocess.
fields.Note: Taglish (mixed Tagalog/English) is not addressed anywhere in Gong's docs.

fields.What: Email labels, red-flag alerts, Gong-recommended to-dos and example-based smart trackers are English only; question-based smart trackers work in all languages; Gong Assistant answers in the question's language.

features.name: AI translation of transcripts and briefs

fields.What: Transcripts, summaries and call/contact/account/deal briefs translate from any language; per-source-language auto-translate preference or on demand; admin defaults; translated summaries can export to CRM.

Per-workspace terms with classification (our company / another company / general) and comma-separated mis-transcriptions per language. Applies to new calls immediately and to history within hours; only transcript text changes, AI outputs are not regenerated.
fields.Note: Product names and local place names will mis-transcribe; cheap to build, high value.

fields.What: Interface in English, French, Canadian French and Korean; rolling out.

decisions: **Which languages must v1 handle?** If reps speak Taglish at the door, test your STT engine on real recordings before committing; Gong publishes nothing about code-switching.
unverified: **Transcription accuracy figures.** Not published in the articles read.
**Retention of raw audio vs transcript.** See M33.

name: Call page, player & collaboration
intro: The call page is the product's centre of gravity: a player with per-speaker isolation, a talk-time bar, transcript/outline/call-info panels, AI briefs on top, and comments and scoring on the right. Everything else (coaching, deals, search) deep-links into a moment on this page.

features.name: Processing state on the call page

fields.What: While media is prepared the page shows 'Processing call media'; briefs, transcript and playback appear when done.
fields.Api: Realtime subscription on the call row

fields.What: Skip ±15 s, playback speed, isolate one speaker's sections, scrub the timeline to jump.
fields.Data: Signed URL to media in Storage; speaker segments from `transcript_segments`
fields.Ui: Centered player, speed menu, speaker filter.

fields.What: Bar under the player showing when each participant spoke; pick a participant to listen only to them.
Speaker-attributed text; click a line to seek; in-panel search highlights matches. Translated transcripts aren't searchable.
AI-generated timestamped section summary; click a heading to jump.

features.name: Call info and points of interest

fields.What: Attendees, date, duration, classification, CRM associations; correct speaker names; manual CRM association. Points of interest auto-flag questions asked, competitor mentions, pricing discussions and filler words as timeline markers.
fields.Ui: Call info tab; markers on timeline.

fields.What: Click the title to rename; edit participant details in Call Info.

features.name: Timestamped comments with mentions and visibility

fields.What: Comment on a moment; @mention colleagues (they're notified and see it under Home > Collaboration > Received, plus email/Slack per settings); visibility: everyone, specific people, or only me; edit/delete. Hashtags are searchable.

Share with colleagues plus a message; they get a notification and need an account to view.
fields.Data: `call_shares(id, call_id, shared_by, kind='internal', recipient_user_id, message)`; also grants `call_user_access`

fields.What: Customer-facing link for the full call or a snippet; admin caps expiry at up to 100 days; 'anyone with link' (identity via Google or LinkedIn) or 'only specific people' from approved domains after email verification; full-call shares can include Highlights and Outline.
For external shares, a Shares & Views tab lists share details and view activity.
Drag yellow bars to select a portion; share, comment, save to library, download or embed the snippet. Recipients see only that part; original untouched.
fields.Note: In your context: 'best objection handle this week' clips for the team.

fields.What: Embed code for internal wikis (viewer must be signed in and permitted); 'copy embed link' for non-users gives the player without transcript or summaries.
Download media or transcript; needs 'Download call media'.

features.name: Listen later and add to library

fields.What: Top-right actions save the call to 'Listen later' or a library folder.

Owner or tech admin trims a section; it disappears from playback, transcript and AI outputs after reprocessing. Original restorable within six months of the recording date (triggers reanalysis). Existing customer links are not revoked.
fields.Data: `call_trims(call_id, start_ms, end_ms, trimmed_by, at)`; keep original media until `recorded_at + 6 months`

fields.What: Removes recording, transcript, comments, scores, notes, stats, related tasks and the CRM conversation record. No recovery. Bulk delete is tech-admin only.
fields.Note: Deleting a scored call also deletes its points in your gamification model unless points are stored separately — a design decision in M15.

fields.What: Restrict access without removing content; owners need 'set owned calls as private'.
Reps take notes during a recorded call that attach to it. Basis: 'Take notes during a call' article in index; content not read.

unverified: **Comment replies and reactions.** Not covered in the collaboration article.
**Who may set a call private and its effect on stats.** Not stated.

name: Interaction stats & team insights
intro: Gong computes a small, fixed set of conversation-mechanics stats per call (talk ratio, longest monologue, longest customer story, interactivity, patience, question rate) and publishes benchmarks for them. The Insights > Team page rolls them up by manager, period and call category.

fields.What: Share of the call the rep speaks; computed per call then averaged. Benchmark ~43% rep for top-converting B2B calls.
fields.Note: Gong's benchmark is B2B; a door pitch will have different norms. Don't import the number as a target.

fields.What: Longest uninterrupted rep stretch per call; benchmark ≤2:30.
Longest uninterrupted customer stretch; shows whether they could share needs. Company-level stat (same for everyone on the call).

How often speech switches between company and external side, counted per 5-minute block and averaged; capped at 10; brief acknowledgements don't count; benchmark ≥5. Only calls scoring 1–10 with talk ratio 1–99% are included.
Rep's pause after the customer stops before responding; median per call, then averaged; benchmark 0.6–1.0 s.
fields.Api: Gap between external end and rep start

fields.What: Rep questions scaled to an hour; benchmark ≥18/hour.
Average call duration, weekly call volume, weekly hours on calls, total call volume and total time per person in period.
Fast team response (% answered within 24 h), team response time (excl. >7 days), team response rate (% within 7 days); auto-replies and thank-yous excluded.
Pick a manager's team or several teams/members, period and call category; toggle Individuals (row per person) and Attended (include calls joined, not just hosted); click a row for that person.
